review_notes: The article states that the current Jyotinagar failure is the third large landslide in the area and mixes the current slide with earlier/recurrent failures. The earlier two cannot be individually located or dated, so a complete physical-event mapping is not defensible.

The article establishes six separate landslides, but only one is individually located; the other five are collectively described between Paduka and Sangetada. Creating six indistinguishable group objects would invent identity details, while collapsing them would violate the one-physical-event rule.

The article explicitly says two landslides fell overnight at/around Hiyunde Khola, but it does not distinguish the two physical failures or give enough separate location/date evidence to map them without inventing identity details.
